papers.abstract_en: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) affects a large portion of the global population but remains substantially underdiagnosed due to limited access to polysomnography. While machine learning has shown promise for scalable OSA screening, many recent models rely on overnight physiological monitoring and are not validated across heterogeneous cohorts. This study develops and evaluates questionnaire-based CatBoost models for OSA detection using two large, multi-cohort datasets (SHHS and WSC). The models use 42 easily obtainable features that require no specialized equipment, which could potentially enable highly accessible screening. We assessed performance through comprehensive internal and external validation, including within-cohort external testing (SHHS1 →  SHHS2) and cross-cohort generalization (SHHS1 →  WSC1), across three clinically relevant AHI cutoffs ( ≥  5, ≥  15, ≥  30 events/h). In internal validation, models achieved consistently balanced performance with AUC 0.74-0.76, sensitivity 67%-73%, and specificity 62%-70% across all cutoffs. Performance remained stable during within-cohort external testing at cutoff ≥  15 (AUC 0.75, sensitivity 71%, specificity 65%). However, cross-cohort validation revealed noticeable performance degradation due to population distribution shifts, most pronounced at ≥  5 where specificity dropped substantially (48.5% ±  4.7%) when models trained on the older SHHS cohort were applied to the younger WSC population. SHAP analysis confirmed that predictions relied primarily on established clinical risk factors including neck circumference, age, BMI, and symptom history. These results demonstrate that questionnaire-based machine learning can achieve more balanced sensitivity-specificity trade-offs than traditional scoring rules, and highlight the importance of multi-cohort external testing.

papers.abstract_en: Quantifying T cell response during primary infection in humans is crucial for understanding adaptive immunity. Leveraging a controlled human challenge to severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2, we characterized antigen-specific T cell responses within and across individuals. Notably, individual clones reached similar maximum frequencies despite differences in the timing of their peak expansion. Mathematical modeling within a coarse-grained framework suggested that variability in precursor frequency between different T cell clones could be one mechanism to explain this relationship. Single-cell profiling revealed distinct temporal programs for CD4+ and CD8+ T cells, with CD4+ cells expanding earlier but contracting to a lower frequency. Clones with similar receptors, likely recognizing the same antigen, expanded at similar times. Together, these findings highlight how clone-intrinsic properties such as precursor frequency and CD4/CD8 subset status shape T cell clonal kinetics. papers.authors: Li T, Yu Y, Liu C, Liu Z, Tan Q, Li W
papers.affiliation_highlight: Intensive Care Unit (ICU), Department of Cardiac Surgery, Shandong Provincial Hospital Affiliated to Shandong First Medi…
papers.results: 共分析出HAP病例1938例（31.278%）。PM10、O3、PM2.5、SO2日均浓度分别为120、75、59、25 μg/m³，CO平均0.979 mg/m³。PM2.5与HAP的关联在围术期暴露窗lag 1天具有统计学意义：PM2.5浓度30 μg/m³与参考浓度10 μg/m³相比，HAP比值高14.2%（95%CI: 2.6–27%）。分层分析显示≥60岁老年人、BMI>23.9 kg/m²患者及糖尿病患者关联更强。进一步调整机械通气时长等临床协变量后，观察到的暴露-反应关联的稳健性得到确认。
papers.authors_conclusion: These findings revealed a substantial and robust link between short-term PM2.5 exposure and elevated HAP incidence in the vulnerable population undergoing cardiovascular surgeries.
papers.ai_note: 暴露为地区日均环境浓度而非个体实际暴露，属生态层面关联，残余混杂与因果推断限制明显；lag 1天为显著滞后点，摘要未说明是否在多个滞后日中择优报告、也未见整体暴露窗检验的全局P值，存在选择性强调次要/单点结果的可能；VAP未单独分析，HAP终点可能混合入院即存在与呼吸机相关成分，与标题的'医院获得性肺炎'口径存在界定模糊；亚组（年龄、BMI、糖尿病）为分层结果，未见多重比较校正；主模型混杂调整主要为污染物、时间趋势与气象，临床个体层面协变量为'额外调整'，提示核心模型可能存在残余临床混杂；样本为心脏手术患者，与胸部肿瘤外科核心业务关联有限。信息不足：摘要未给出滞后结构的整体检验与模型拟合细节。

pico.p: 2014年1月1日至2023年12月31日在山东省某大医院ICU接受心血管手术的患者6196例
pico.ic: 以环境日均PM2.5浓度为暴露（30 μg/m³ 对比参考浓度10 μg/m³），对照为低浓度参考水平；结局为按CDC/NHSN标准定义的医院获得性肺炎（HAP），VAP未作为独立终点分析

papers.reason: 为ICU术后肺炎这一脆弱人群提供环境空气污染可干预性风险的定量证据（PM2.5 30 vs 10 μg/m³对应14.2% HAP风险升高），可为心脏及胸外科术后ICU的感染防控、季节性高污染时段管理与患者沟通提供参考，同时其暴露测量与滞后选择方式可作为同类环境-感染研究设计的对照案例
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Ambient air pollution (AAP) exposure is a substantial health threat to humans globally. However, whether AAP could promote hospital-acquired pneumonia (HAP) onset in critically ill patients, a vulnerable population undergoing cardiac surgery in the intensive care unit (ICU), remains elusive. This study evaluated the correlation of HAP onset with fine particulate matter (PM2.5). METHODS: In total, this study included 6,196 patients who underwent cardiovascular surgery at the ICU of a major hospital in Shandong province, China, over 10 years, from January 1, 2014, to December 31, 2023. The daily mean levels of sulfur dioxide (SO2), PM2.5, carbon monoxide (CO), PM10, and ozone (O3) were assessed from publicly available data. The outcome was HAP, defined according to CDC/NHSN pneumonia criteria as pneumonia developing >48 h after hospital admission and not present or incubating at admission; VAP was not analyzed as a separate endpoint. The association between PM2.5 and HAP was estimated via a distributed lag non-linear model, adjusted for pollutants, time trends, and weather conditions. RESULTS: This study analyzed 1938 (31.278%) HAP cases. The mean levels of PM10, O3, PM2.5, and SO2 were 120, 75, 59, and 25 μg/m3, respectively, and the mean CO level was 0.979 mg/m3. The association between PM2.5 and HAP was statistically significant at lag 1 day within the perioperative exposure window. At a PM2.5 concentration of 30 μg/m3 compared with the reference concentration of 10 μg/m3, 14.2% higher odds of HAP were observed (95% CI: 2.6-27%). The stratified analyses indicated stronger associations among elders aged ≥ 60 years, patients with body mass index (BMI) > 23.9 kg/m2 and patients with diabetes. Additional adjustment for clinical covariates, including duration of mechanical ventilation, confirmed the robustness of the observed exposure-response association. CONCLUSION: These findings revealed a substantial and robust link between short-term PM2.5 exposure and elevated HAP incidence in the vulnerable population undergoing cardiovascular surgeries.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Anaesthetic drugs used during the perioperative period may influence surgical outcomes in cancer patients. Recently, remimazolam besylate, a rapid-onset and ultra-short-acting sedative, has been introduced for sedation and anaesthesia maintenance. This study aimed to assess its potential anti-cancer effects on human lung carcinoma cells (A549) in vitro and in vivo, and to explore the underlying mechanisms. METHODS: Cultured A549 lung cancer cells were exposed to remimazolam besylate (0.1 to 500 μM) for up to 24 hours and their viability was assessed with the CCK-8 assay. The effects of remimazolam besylate on cancer cell proliferation, migration, mitochondrial mass, and apoptosis were assessed through RNA sequencing and immunofluorescence staining. Tumour growth was evaluated in a xenograft model of Balb/c nude mice after treatment with 5 mg/kg of remimazolam besylate via intraperitoneal injection for 21 consecutive days. Its cytotoxicity was also assessed with cultured HK-2 normal kidney cells. RESULTS: Remimazolam besylate significantly inhibited cell viability at 200 μM (61.2 ± 12.7 vs 103.8 ± 6.0, P = 0.003) and 300 μM (46 ± 10 vs 95 ± 21, P = 0.02). It suppressed migration (56.38 ± 3.06 vs 85.10 ± 10.84, P = 0.03) and reduced mitochondrial mass (63.5 ± 24.9 vs 150.5 ± 55.9, P = 0.02). Additionally, it increased caspase-3 and cleaved caspase-9 expression, and reduced tumour size by 74.6% compared to the control (P = 0.002). The 50% concentration of cytotoxicity (IC50) for remimazolam besylate in A549 cells was found to be 297.5 μM, whereas the IC50 for HK-2 cells was predicted to be significantly higher at 2,200 μM. CONCLUSION: Remimazolam besylate primarily and preferentially inhibits human lung carcinoma cells. It induces apoptosis associated with endoplasmic reticulum stress and cell death signaling pathways.

papers.authors: Alimu A, Xu J, Gong H, Abudureheman Z, Tuersun A, Xue L, Lu X, Li L et al.

papers.results: ExWAS分析识别出8项与结核风险相关的环境暴露；AENET模型选出5项作为预测因子：PM₁₀、PM₂.₅、NO₂与结核风险正相关（OR=1.013、OR=1.008、OR=1.018，p<0.0001），风速与相对湿度与结核风险负相关（OR=0.983、OR=0.944，p<0.0001）；在环境因素中，XGBoost模型识别PM₁₀为与结核相关的最重要因素。摘要未报告95%CI。

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: To explore associations between ambient air pollutants, meteorological factors and pulmonary tuberculosis risk among residents in Kashi, China METHODS : Data on TB cases were collected from the Data Platform, while data on non-TB controls were retrieved from the hospital electronic medical record system. Exposome-wide association study (ExWAS) was used to explore the association between single factor exposure and TB risk, Adaptive Elastic-net (AENET) penalty regression method was used to construct a multi-factor regression model of TB risk, Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) method ranked the relative important factors of TB risk . RESULTS: The ExWAS analysis identified eight environmental exposures association with TB risk. Five of the exposures were selected as predictors by the AENET model: particulate matter 10 and 2.5 (PM10, PM2.5), nitrogen dioxide(NO2) (OR = 1.013, OR = 1.008, OR = 1.018, p < 0.0001) were positively associated with the TB risk, while wind velocity and relative humidity (OR = 0.983, OR = 0.944, p < 0.0001) were negatively associated with TB risk. Among environmental factors, the XGBoost model identified PM₁₀ as the most important factor associated with TB. CONCLUSION: Exposure to PM₁₀, PM₂.₅, NO₂ were positive correlated with TB risk, while wind velocity and relative humidity were negatively correlated. Environmental factors should be prioritized in TB prevention strategies.

papers.abstract_en: Seasonal influenza remains a major global public health burden. Although environmental exposures have been implicated in influenza transmission, the effects of exposure to air pollution mixtures on influenza, as well as the potential modifying role of vaccination, remain insufficiently understood. We conducted a multi-city time-series study across 11 prefecture-level cities in Shanxi Province, northern China, using daily data from 2014 to 2022. Information on influenza incidence, ambient air pollutant concentrations, meteorological variables, and influenza vaccination was collected. A two-stage time-series framework integrating distributed lag nonlinear models with meta-analysis was applied, using city-specific zero-inflated negative binomial models with lag periods of 0-7 days. Multi-pollutant mixture effects were assessed using weighted quantile sum (WQS) regression and Quantile g-Computation (qgcomp) models. Effect modification by influenza vaccination was further examined. In single-pollutant analyses, each 10 μg/m3 increase in PM2.5, PM10, and NO2 and each 1 mg/m3 increase in CO were associated with relative risks of influenza of 1.024 (95% CI: 1.015-1.034), 1.018 (95% CI: 1.010-1.025), 1.115 (95% CI: 1.086-1.146), and 1.095 (95% CI: 1.024-1.171), respectively. Both WQS and qgcomp analyses indicated significant positive mixture effects, with SO2 and NO2 contributing most to the overall association (WQS RR =1.078, 95% CI: 1.005-1.157; qgcomp RR =1.122, 95% CI:1.064-1.182). Exploratory analyses suggested potential effect modification by city-level vaccination coverage, particularly for PM2.5 and CO. Exposure to air pollution mixtures was associated with increased population susceptibility to influenza, while vaccination coverage may attenuate pollution-related risks, underscoring the need to consider environmental exposures alongside immunization strategies in highly polluted settings.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Routine whole-genome sequencing (WGS) interpretation of Mycobacterium tuberculosis resistance focuses mainly on consensus-level mutations. Minority variants, quantified by allele frequency (AF), may indicate resistant subpopulations under drug pressure, but their association with treatment response in rifampicin-resistant or multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (RR/MDR-TB) remains unclear. METHODS: We retrospectively analysed RR/MDR-TB patients treated in Ningbo, China, from 2021 to 2025, integrating clinical, phenotypic, treatment, microbiological, and WGS data. Minority resistance-associated variants (RAVs) were defined as low-frequency variants matching WHO V2 mutation catalogue entries at AF ≥ 3%, with AF ≥ 5% defining the primary higher-frequency subset. Per-drug analyses excluded patients whose target genes had median depth <200×. Associations with microbiological response were assessed using covariate-adjusted logistic regression, with higher-frequency and treatment-matched variants examined secondarily. RESULTS: We analysed 229 RR/MDR-TB patients with linked WGS, treatment, and microbiological follow-up data. Fixed RAVs (WHO V2 catalogue-annotated) were carried by 220/229 patients (median 3, IQR 2-5). Minority RAVs at AF ≥ 3% were detected in 13 patients. Overall minority-RAV burden was not clearly associated with microbiological response after adjustment. The clearest signal involved treatment-matched AF ≥ 5% minority RAVs, whose carriers had a higher 6-month culture-positivity rate than non-carriers (4/7 [57.1%] vs 40/198 [20.2%]; adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 7.21, 95% CI 1.38-43.68; p = 0.020; q = 0.034), with a modest AUC increase from 0.675 to 0.695. Six-month positivity was highest among patients with both high fixed RAV burden and treatment-matched AF ≥ 5% minority RAVs (4/5 [80.0%] vs 15/106 [14.2%] in the low-burden non-carrier reference; Fisher's exact p = 0.003). CONCLUSION: Minority variants showed limited overall prognostic value, but higher-frequency treatment-matched variants provided a coherent signal for 6-month culture positivity when considered with fixed RAV burden. These exploratory findings support a cautious, treatment-aware review of selected minority variants and require external validation before clinical use.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Current or former smokers with a 20-pack-year history between the ages of 50 and 80 years are eligible for lung cancer screening (LCS) under current guidelines. Despite age restrictions for screening, older patients remain at risk for lung cancer and, without screening, are diagnosed with advanced-stage disease that limits curative treatment options.Treatment for early-stage lung cancer has improved with minimally invasive surgical techniques and reduced toxicity associated with stereotactic body radiation therapy. Robust older patients can tolerate surgical resection or stereotactic body radiation therapy with rates of recovery similar to those of their younger peers. Given the advancements in treatment and the improved tools available to identify frailty, chronological age should not be a gatekeeper for LCS. METHODS: A taskforce within the International Society of Geriatric Oncology was created to address challenges of LCS within older patients. Taskforce members represented five different specialties with clinical expertise in lung cancer and the care of older adults. RESULTS: For patients above 80 years old who qualify for LCS, we recommend performing a geriatric assessment (GA) to assess functional status and age-related vulnerabilities. Robust patients, as determined by GA, should be eligible for screening and discuss their health care priorities in shared decision-making conversations. GA should be performed every 2 years while patients are enrolled in LCS to determine the appropriateness of continued screening efforts. CONCLUSIONS: Age should not be an exclusion criterion for LCS. Patients above 80 years old should be thoughtfully co-managed by geriatric and lung cancer specialists to determine which older patients would benefit from screening efforts.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Comprehensive genomic profiling is increasingly recognized as the standard for predictive biomarker testing in non-small cell lung carcinoma (NSCLC). However, resource-constrained settings face challenges with universal upfront next-generation sequencing (NGS) because of limitations in infrastructure, cost, tissue adequacy, and turnaround time. AIMS: To assess the feasibility, diagnostic yield, and limitations of a staggered reflex biomarker testing workflow integrating single-gene testing (SGT) and targeted NGS. METHODS: This retrospective audit included consecutive treatment-naïve NSCLC patients from March 2025 to March 2026. Samples with tumor fraction < 20% underwent SGT only, whereas those with tumor fraction ≥ 20% underwent SGT followed by targeted 40-gene DNA/RNA NGS if negative for EGFR, ALK, and ROS1. Diagnostic yield, testing attrition, and actionable genomic alterations were evaluated. RESULTS: Of 867 patient samples, 534 (61.6%) entered the staggered workflow. SGT identified EGFR, ALK, or ROS1 alterations in 172 (32.2%). Among 362 triple-negative cases, 127 (35.1%) failed pre-library DNA and/or RNA quantity/quality requirements, and 235 (64.9%) underwent NGS. Clinically actionable alterations beyond those detected by SGT were detected in 64/235 (27.2%) patients. Overall, clinically actionable alterations were identified in 348/867 (40.1%) patients, while tissue inadequacy or molecular testing failure prevented complete biomarker evaluation in another 348 867 (40.1%) patients. KRAS was the most frequent oncogenic driver beyond EGFR/ALK/ROS1, followed by ERBB2, MET, and RET. CONCLUSION: NGS identified clinically actionable alterations in over one-quarter of patients negative for EGFR, ALK, and ROS1. Staggered testing is a practical strategy for integrating NGS in resource-limited settings, with SGT as a reliable fallback when NGS fails.

papers.abstract_en: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains the predominant subtype of lung cancer and a leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide. Therapeutic failure is largely driven by intratumoral heterogeneity, dynamic tumor microenvironmental stresses, and adaptive drug resistance. Unlike previous reviews focusing on isolated lncRNA-target axes, this review proposes an integrated conceptual framework emphasizing that four major classes of tumor-associated stresses are highly interconnected through a cross-stress compensatory network. Within this framework, lncRNAs serve as central yet functionally stratified regulatory nodes bridging stress sensing and adaptive reprogramming. We propose a functional continuum rather than a fixed binary classification: stress-sensing and downstream effector lncRNAs represent relative positions along a stress-input-to-adaptive-output axis, and the same lncRNA may switch or combine these roles depending on cell type, genetic background, stress intensity, and treatment context. We systematically illustrate how stress-responsive lncRNAs reshape metabolic reprogramming, redox homeostasis, ferroptosis susceptibility, immune evasion, autophagy, DNA-damage repair, and therapeutic resistance. We further show that these four stress conditions do not operate in isolation; rather, metabolites, ROS, hypoxia-responsive signaling, and intercellular communication generate reciprocal feedback and cross-compensation that together sustain tumor survival under sustained pressure. Beyond mechanistic integration, we discuss the translational prospects of stress-related lncRNAs as diagnostic and prognostic biomarkers, therapeutic targets, and mediators for mechanism-based combination therapies. However, it is critical to note that no lncRNA-targeting therapeutic agent has yet entered clinical trials for NSCLC, and the path from bench to bedside remains constrained by delivery challenges, model fidelity limitations, and insufficient standardization of clinical assays. Comprehensive dissection of lncRNA-mediated stress-adaptation networks will deepen our understanding of NSCLC pathogenesis and facilitate the development of precision medicine strategies.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: In patients requiring mechanical ventilation, normal aerosol dynamics are disrupted by the artificial airway, circuit configuration and humidification systems. These factors can result in substantial drug losses within the ventilator circuit and markedly lower lung deposition than during spontaneous breathing, thereby potentially limiting therapeutic efficacy. A mechanistic proof-of-concept study using an in silico model has been conducted to evaluate aerosol deposition in the lung under differing delivery flow profiles. METHODS: Digital Twinhale® technology was used to generate a subject-specific whole-lung model from CT-derived airway and lung geometry data from a healthy adult, using a 16-generation airway tree and calibrated physiological parameters. Aerosol transport was simulated with three-dimensional Lagrangian particle dynamics using in vitro droplet properties. Phase 1 of the study evaluated Aerogen vibrating mesh nebuliser (A-VMN), jet nebuliser (JN) and pressurised metered dose inhaler (pMDI) use under identical delivery flow profiles to assess the impact of the device on delivery efficiency and deposition patterns. In the second phase, deposition via VMN was assessed under two representative simulation scenarios: B1, a sinusoidal (volume controlled ventilation-like) waveform, and B2, a rectangular pressure (pressure controlled ventilation-like) waveform, using matched respiratory settings, including respiratory rate, inhalation-to-exhalation ratio and nominal tidal volume. RESULTS: Digital modelling allowed observation of differences in device performance, with the A-VMN yielding the highest deposited mass fraction across all lobes and lung regions, as well as the greatest level of functional deposition within the alveolar airways. Modelling ventilator mode-like inspiratory flow profiles allowed the observation that the highest deposited mass fraction was obtained with the B1 flow profile, whereas use of B2 resulted in a greater proportion of the emitted dose being lost to exhalation. Overall, differing flow profile had little effect on central-to-peripheral ratios, indicating that deposition patterns were mainly influenced by aerosol characteristics rather than differences in delivered dose or ventilation parameters. CONCLUSIONS: These findings support the feasibility of using a patient-specific in silico whole-lung model to compare predicted aerosol deposition under controlled conditions. However, further validation in multi-subject models and clinical studies will be required to determine whether these predicted deposition differences translate into meaningful clinical benefit.

papers.abstract_en: Cystic fibrosis (CF) is a disorder caused by mutations in the CF transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) gene, which result in impaired expression and function of the channel that is regulated by cAMP intracellular levels. Therefore, cAMP-elevating agents have been investigated for the treatment of CF, including phosphodiesterase (PDE) inhibitors that act by preventing its degradation by PDE enzymes. Here we characterized the effects of the novel inhaled PDE4 inhibitor, tanimilast (CHF6001), designed to overcome PDE inhibitors systemic adverse effects, on CFTR activation by measuring short-circuit current (Isc) in cellular models expressing native and F508del CFTR (CFBE41o- and normal human bronchial epithelial cells: MucilAir™). Various PDE4 genes (PDE4A, B, D) are expressed in both cell models to different extents. Tanimilast was able to increase Isc in a concentration-dependent manner in both cell models, peaking at 0.2 μM in MucilAir™ expressing either WT and F508del CFTR corrected with a combination of VX445 and VX661 for 24 h. Taken together, these results indicate for the first time that the PDE4 inhibitor tanimilast could enhance, in vitro, the effects of CFTR correctors used in clinical practice.

papers.abstract_en: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) can trigger autoimmune and autoinflammatory toxicities through disruption of peripheral immune tolerance. Relapsing polychondritis (RP) after programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) blockade is rare and are described mainly in individual reports. We report a 66-year-old man who developed severe airway-predominant RP after 10 cycles of pembrolizumab for lung adenocarcinoma. Chest CT showed new diffuse tracheal and bilateral bronchial wall thickening and calcification, with severe obstructive ventilatory impairment and systemic inflammation. Exploratory serial peripheral-blood immunophenotyping demonstrated increased proportions of CD38+ and HLA-DR+ cells among circulating CD8+ T cells early in the disease course. Serial measurements showed lower activated CD8+ T-cell proportions during immunosuppressive treatment, in parallel with partial stabilization of respiratory symptoms, pulmonary function and imaging. The patient received sequential glucocorticoids, tofacitinib, methotrexate, abatacept and tocilizumab. Despite partial inflammatory control, subsequent pulmonary infection with severe coughing was followed by pneumomediastinum and progressive structural airway compromise requiring bilateral main-bronchial stenting. One year after stenting, the stents remained in situ with no obvious luminal stenosis and pulmonary function remained stable. This case extends the reported spectrum of pembrolizumab-associated RP by documenting an airway-predominant, treatment refractory course with serial immune phenotyping and long-term post-stenting follow-up.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Chlamydia psittaci pneumonia (CPP) is a rare disease that is difficult to diagnose. Its clinical manifestations and chest imaging findings often overlap with those of other types of community-acquired pneumonia (CAP), and nonspecific treatment is likely to lead to rapid disease progression. This study aimed to explore the clinical and radiological differences between CPP and CAP. METHODS: We enrolled 29 patients with non-severe CPP diagnosed using metagenomic next-generation sequencing, as well as 87 with CAP, who had been diagnosed between December 2019 and September 2023. The demographic, clinical, and radiological characteristics of CPP were analyzed and compared with those of CAP. RESULTS: Compared to the patients with CAP, those with non-severe CPP were more likely to experience fever (P = 0.034), headache (P = 0.009), asthenia (P<0.001), abnormal auscultation of the lungs (P = 0.020), and abnormal laboratory examination results-including lymphocyte count (P = 0.002), C-reactive protein (P = 0.001), aspartate aminotransferase (P<0.001), alanine aminotransferase (P<0.001), and creatine kinase levels (P<0.001). Regarding radiological characteristics, CPP predominantly showed unilateral (P = 0.003) and single-lobar (P = 0.004) involvement, whereas CAP commonly exhibited bilateral and multi-lobar involvement. CPP was more likely to be associated with air bronchograms (P = 0.026), interlobular septal thickening (P = 0.001), and bronchovascular bundle thickening (P<0.001) than CAP was. CONCLUSIONS: Clinical epidemiology, laboratory examination, and radiological characteristics are useful for diagnosing and differentiating CPP from CAP.

papers.abstract_en: Influenza A/H5Nx viruses continue to diversify and undergo gene reassortment as they infect avian and mammalian hosts worldwide. The severity of human infections varies substantially between different H5 clades and neuraminidase (NA) reassortants, creating unpredictable pandemic risk. Existing H5 vaccines, typically based on a single hemagglutinin (HA) strain, cannot keep pace with this natural variation. To address this problem, we computationally engineer HA, NA, and M2 antigens representing the global antigenic space of circulating H5Nx viruses, prioritizing N1 and N6 subtypes associated with the highest threat in humans. The resulting digitally immune-optimized mRNA vaccine, DVX-panH5Nx, elicits broad HA neutralization and NA inhibition across divergent clades in mice and ferrets. Compared to WHO candidate vaccine viruses (CVVs), DVX-panH5Nx confers superior protection against antigenically distinct H5N1 challenges spanning two decades of viral evolution, demonstrating that computationally designed multivalent antigen vaccines can overcome natural influenza diversification and provide a scalable strategy for pre-pandemic preparedness.

papers.abstract_en: Metabolic constraints, including hypoxia, lactate, and adenosine that impair CD8+ T-cell function and mitochondrial fitness, are increasingly recognized as contributors to resistance to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) in driver-negative (lacking an established first-line actionable driver alteration) advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). We propose a hypothesis-driven framework asking whether transient tissue-level metabolic relief can be temporally aligned with the slower process of T-cell reinvigoration driven by immune checkpoint blockade (ICB). Its mechanistic basis is a lactate-mitochondrial axis linking extracellular metabolic suppression to mitochondrial states in tumor-infiltrating T cells, with T-cell-intrinsic mitochondrial adaptation treated as a testable extension. Locoregional mild hyperthermia (39-42 °C) is conceptualized as a transient modulator of tissue-level metabolic gradients rather than a direct immune activator. Because oxygenation, metabolite distribution, and acid-base status may change independently or in opposing directions, oxygenation is treated as a physiological readout rather than a surrogate for metabolic relief. We define a relief window as transient attenuation of hypoxic constraint accompanied by redistribution of lactate and adenosine away from T-cell-containing regions. Because such windows are short relative to ICB-driven reinvigoration, their therapeutic relevance may depend on recurrent temporal overlap, quantified through coverage and placement using provisional criteria at graded levels of evidence. The framework is proposed to apply primarily to glycolytic, hypoxic tumors retaining reinvigoration-competent progenitor exhausted T cells, with KRAS/STK11 co-mutant and KEAP1-altered NSCLC prioritized for testing as indicators of metabolic phenotype rather than predictors of benefit, subject to baseline confirmation that a reinvigoration-competent T-cell compartment is present. We specify necessary conditions, enabling requirements, and failure conditions, together with safety monitoring for repeated heating, while treating local-to-systemic immune propagation as an optional extension. A phase 0 strategy is proposed to establish whether reproducible candidate relief windows can be detected in patients, before efficacy testing and before any inference of clinical benefit.

papers.abstract_en: Asthma is a heterogeneous chronic airway disease. Asthma endotypes are mainly classified as type 2-high and type 2-low, based on immunological and molecular mechanisms, providing a more comprehensive framework for understanding the underlying pathological processes. Airway epithelial cells (AECs) and lung macrophages contribute to airway homeostasis and asthmatic inflammation through communication that can support either tissue protection or disease-associated responses. This narrative review integrates their physiological and pathological functions, focusing on AEC-to-macrophage and macrophage-to-AEC signaling within broader multicellular networks across different asthma endotypes. Direct functional evidence for intercellular communication from associations and indirect mechanisms is distinguished and graded. Therapeutic strategies targeting AECs, lung macrophages, and their crosstalk, including both clinically validated and preclinical approaches, are also discussed. The AEC-macrophage axis exhibits context-dependent signaling that may amplify inflammation or support protective regulation, providing a basis for evaluating potential therapeutic interventions.

papers.abstract_en: Maternal vaccination is a powerful tool for protecting the health of mothers and infants but the role of surveillance systems in supporting vaccination programme design and implementation is underexplored. This paper considers how surveillance and post-implementation monitoring have helped to shape the timing and rationale for introduction of, and progressive change in, maternal pertussis vaccination in seven high-income European nations (England, Finland, France, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands and Spain). We show that differences in surveillance system design and in programme decision-making have had important implications for both timing of introduction and programme structure in each country, but that contingency has been a key factor especially where countries introduced vaccination as an outbreak response measure. papers.abstract_en: Pulmonary embolism (PE) is one of the most severe manifestations of venous thromboembolism, yet current diagnostic and preventive frameworks have largely been developed in ground-based clinical settings. Deep underground environments represent complex occupational exposure systems characterized by relative hypoxia or oxygen fluctuation, normobaric to mildly hyperbaric pressure, high humidity and heat, airborne particulates, radon accumulation, restricted ventilation, limited mobility, circadian disruption, and enclosed psychosocial stress. These factors may interact dynamically with oxygen sensing, cardiopulmonary compensation, venous return, endothelial function, and coagulation-inflammation pathways. However, the relationship between deep underground exposure, thrombogenesis, PE recognition, and prevention remains insufficiently conceptualized. Direct epidemiological evidence linking deep-underground occupational exposure to incident venous thromboembolism or PE remains scarce, and existing PE prediction tools have not been specifically validated in deep-underground occupational populations. Therefore, this review does not assume that underground exposure independently increases PE incidence or that established clinical tools are inadequate. Instead, we develop a hypothesis-driven framework to examine whether exposure-related factors-including oxygen fluctuation, heat and dehydration, restricted mobility, altered hemodynamics, and inflammatory stress-could modify thrombotic susceptibility, symptom interpretation, or the operational performance of conventional PE pathways. We summarize the environmental and physiological stressors relevant to PE, examine how they may amplify Virchow's triad, and discuss research questions concerning symptom recognition, anticoagulation, reperfusion decision-making, preventive interventions, and the staged development of dynamic risk warning models. This review aims to provide a conceptual foundation for future surveillance, prevention, and clinical research on PE in deep underground occupational populations.

CONCLUSION: These findings may clarify the regulatory mechanisms of sodium channels in ARDS associated with chronic alcohol consumption.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Circular RNAs (circRNAs) have emerged as important regulators of diverse cellular processes, and accumulating evidence indicates that certain circRNAs modulate immune responses through complex mechanisms. However, their roles in innate immunity against influenza A virus (IAV) infection remain poorly understood. METHODS: We identified a previously uncharacterized circRNA, termed circMARCH3, through RNA-seq, RNase R digestion assay, and RNA stability assay. We examined circMARCH3 expression in multiple cell types following viral infection by RT-PCR and real-time PCR, investigated the signaling pathway driving its induction, and performed functional analyses using circMARCH3 overexpression vectors and shRNAs-mediated knockdown. Furthermore, we identified and validated the circMARCH3/miR-3657/ATG7 axis through mechanistic studies. RESULTS: circMARCH3 is generated from the pre-mRNA of the membrane-associated RING-CH-Type Finger 3 (MARCH3) gene, and its expression was robustly induced by IAV and several other viral infections in multiple cell types. Mechanistically, virus-induced circMARCH3 expression was driven by the NF-κB signaling pathway. Functional analyses demonstrated that circMARCH3 overexpression significantly promoted IAV replication, whereas circMARCH3 knockdown markedly inhibited viral production. Consistent with these findings, circMARCH3 functioned as a negative regulator of antiviral innate immunity by attenuating NF-κB activation and type I interferon responses. Furthermore, we identified that circMARCH3 targeted miR-3657, a microRNA that suppresses the expression of ATG7, a key autophagy regulator and known pro-IAV factor. Mechanistic studies revealed that circMARCH3 acted as a competitive endogenous RNA (ceRNA), sequestering miR-3657 and thereby relieving its repressive effect on ATG7 expression, resulting in enhanced autophagy and increased viral replication. DISCUSSION: The results demonstrate circMARCH3 as a virus-inducible circRNA that promotes IAV infection through two complementary mechanisms: dampening NF-κB-mediated antiviral innate immunity and facilitating autophagy via the circMARCH3/miR-3657/ATG7 axis. Our findings establish circMARCH3 as a novel regulator of the complex interaction between host and IAV by coordinating NF-κB negative feedback and the miR-3657/ATG7 axis.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Pseudo-pseudo Meigs syndrome (PPMS), or Tjalma syndrome, is a rare systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE)-associated phenotype characterized by ascites, pleural effusion, and elevated CA125 without an ovarian neoplasm. After assisted reproductive technology (ART), it may overlap with ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (OHSS) or mimic gynecologic malignancy. CASE PRESENTATION: A 25-year-old woman underwent two controlled ovarian stimulation (COS) cycles for intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) because of severe male-factor infertility. Before ART, she had autoimmune thyroid disease and transient urinary abnormalities, but no known SLE. During the second COS cycle, hypertension and albuminuria emerged. Following oocyte retrieval, she developed massive ascites, bilateral pleural effusions, adnexal abnormalities, and marked CA125 elevation, initially raising suspicion of OHSS and ovarian malignancy. Subsequent nephrotic-range proteinuria, profound hypoalbuminemia, hypocomplementemia, and SLE-associated autoantibodies supported active SLE with substantial renal involvement. Cytologic and microbiologic investigations provided no evidence of malignancy or infection. Following SLE-directed treatment, renal abnormalities and serosal effusions improved. At eight months, the adnexal abnormalities had completely resolved and CA125 had normalized, supporting a PPMS phenotype. CONCLUSION: Atypical or persistent post-ART effusions, particularly when accompanied by evolving renal or immunologic abnormalities, should prompt consideration of SLE-associated PPMS as an important differential diagnosis beyond OHSS and gynecologic malignancy. Longitudinal evaluation and multidisciplinary assessment may facilitate timely recognition of this rare phenotype and guide appropriate clinical management.
